title: Supply Chain Planning Microservice

_meta.purpose: Machine-readable PRD for the Supply Chain Planning Microservice (enterprise-supply-chain-planning) flat single-concern microservice foundation; metadata-only scope with explicit non-claims.

goals.scalability: Independent horizontal scaling per ADR-0348 (autosharding/auto-rebalance); tenant- and cell-scoped writes with no shared mutable global state. Foundation scope: metadata-only, no measured scaling evidence.
goals.security: Default-deny tenant isolation via Cedar (ADR-0243) and tenant-as-scope (ADR-0244); no raw credential/PII/secret bytes in the domain. Foundation scope: no runtime authentication.
goals.performance: Per-manifest SLO and capacity targets (ADR-0340) required before any GA claim; async-first eventing on Pulsar. Foundation scope: no measured SLO.
goals.efficiency: FinOps cost attribution (ADR-0344) and flat single-concern crates (ADR-0131/0132) that avoid platform bloat. Foundation scope: no runtime cost telemetry.
goals.reliability: Idempotent metadata operations and rollback-first promotion. Foundation scope: no DR drill evidence.

non_goals: No live demand-sensing ML runtime, planning optimizer, finite scheduler, CTP explosion engine, order backlog rescheduler, transportation execution, or replenishment runtime.

No durable persistence, production order creation, purchase requisition creation, warehouse reservation, inventory mutation, carrier booking, Workflow execution, runtime audit-chain emission, or cloud deployment.
No SAP IBP/APO, Oracle Supply Chain Planning, or Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management exhaustive parity claim.

acceptance_criteria.given: a demand plan has tenant, legal entity, planning area, item, demand location, forecast, firm order, adjustment, horizon, effective date, source refs, and consensus evidence
acceptance_criteria.when: the supply-chain-planning domain approves the demand plan
acceptance_criteria.then: demand plan, tenant, legal entity, planning area, item, location, method, quantities, consensus demand quantity, horizon, effective date, source refs, evidence, idempotency key, state, schema version, and false ML/collaboration/cloud flags are present

acceptance_criteria.given: an approved demand plan is available with on-hand, scheduled receipt, in-transit, safety stock, capacity, lot size, lead time, and planning evidence values
acceptance_criteria.when: supply-network plan proposal metadata is prepared
acceptance_criteria.then: supply plan, demand plan, tenant, legal entity, planning area, item, source and demand locations, demand and supply quantities, net requirement, rounded planned supply, constrained shortage, feasibility flag, evidence, idempotency key, state, and false production/procurement/inventory/cloud flags are present

acceptance_criteria.given: a proposed supply plan is available for an order promise request with requested quantity, available-to-promise quantity, priority, requested ship date, and promise evidence
acceptance_criteria.then: ATP response, supply plan, tenant, legal entity, planning area, item, request location, requested/available/promised/backorder quantities, priority, requested ship date, evidence, idempotency key, state, backorder flag, and false order-management/warehouse/cloud flags are present

acceptance_criteria.given: a proposed supply plan has distribution lane metadata with source/destination locations, transfer quantity, lane capacity, lead time, freight cost, source refs, and lane evidence
acceptance_criteria.then: distribution plan, supply plan, tenant, legal entity, planning area, item, source/destination locations, transfer quantity, lane capacity, remaining capacity, lead time, freight cost, evidence, idempotency key, state, lane sufficiency flag, and false carrier/warehouse/cloud flags are present

acceptance_criteria.given: untrusted identifiers, source refs, evidence refs, dates, horizons, lead times, priority scores, quantities, lane capacities, or overclaim paths enter the supply-chain-planning domain
acceptance_criteria.then: prefix-only identifiers, path traversal, whitespace/control characters, credential-shaped refs, invalid dates, invalid horizons, invalid lead times, zero quantities, invalid priorities, missing demand approval, missing supply-plan proposal, and insufficient lane capacity are refused

decision_log.decision: Supply Chain Planning enters the enterprise microservice set as a flat domain crate rather than an ERP/APO monolith; SAP SCM/APO parity is represented through Tenant RBAC composition while live planning solvers, schedulers, ATP/CTP engines, order-management mutation, inventory and warehouse mutation, carrier booking, Workflow execution, runtime audit emission, and cloud deployment remain explicit non-claims.
